blocks.text: The map records multiplicity and distinctCount summarizes how many keys have positive frequency. Because freq[x] is zero, adding x creates one new distinct value. If that raises distinctCount above K, left removals repair the window until the count returns to K. Repeated copies of an existing x do not change distinctCount. Shrinking before expansion evaluates the old state and can miss the violation introduced by x; clearing the map discards valid overlap. A transient K+1th key is acceptable only long enough to diagnose and repair the post-expansion violation; it is never an answer-eligible state.
